finding.claim: big5 lead-byte range 0xa1-0xfe over-approximates MySQL/MariaDB big5 heads (0xa1-0xf9); writeBufferEscapeMb copies a 0xFA 0x5C pair verbatim so the server treats 0xFA as single byte and the 0x5C as escape, letting a following quote terminate the string (SQL injection via Buffer parameter)
finding.source: Attacker-controlled bytes in a Buffer passed as a ? parameter to Connection.query (text protocol), e.g. Buffer.from(userBase64,'base64')
finding.sink: Text-protocol SQL string built by writeBufferEscapeMb under big5 connection charset

trace.note: Buffer parameter routed to out.writeBufferEscape after '_BINARY ' prefix
same path in TextEncoder for execute-less text encoding
writeBufferEscape bound to writeBufferEscapeMb when getMbRecognizer('big5') matches
isHead(0xFA) true due to charset-mb.js:20 range
length() sees trail 0x5C in 0x40-0x7e -> mbLen 2, pair copied verbatim without escape
next byte 0x27 quote is escaped -> wire bytes FA 5C 5C 27
server (MySQL/MariaDB big5 ismbhead 0xa1-0xf9) reads FA as single byte; 5C 5C is escaped backslash; 27 closes the literal

finding.guards_checked: writeBufferEscapeMb mb-aware path (intended guard) is the code under review; NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES branch (line 689) not active by default; string-level escapeString (utils.js:253) not on this path; execute()/binary protocol unaffected; gbk/sjis/cp932/gb18030 recognizer ranges checked against server lexer and match. finding.claim: For MariaDB servers TLS verification is forced off (connection.js:1350), and the handshake sends the mysql_native_password scramble before the fingerprint/identity check that only runs at OK packet (authentication.js:77-98). A network MITM presenting any self-signed cert and a MariaDB greeting receives the SHA-1 scramble and can crack the password offline.
finding.source: Network attacker on the path to a MariaDB host, client configured with ssl: true (default rejectUnauthorized)
finding.sink: Auth token (native scramble) written to the wire inside the TLS session before server identity is validated

trace.note: isMariaDB() derived from greeting (pre-TLS, attacker controlled), see initial-handshake.js:58-64
rejectUnauthorized forced false for MariaDB
_createSecureContext; selfSignedCertificate = !authorized
gate only rejects non-MITM-proof plugins; native is MITM-proof so it proceeds
NativePasswordAuth.encryptSha1Password(pwd, seed) sent
fingerprint validation deferred until OK packet; throws only after scramble disclosed

finding.guards_checked: Final OK-packet fingerprint validation (rejects the session, but after disclosure); auth-switch cleartext guard authentication.js:309-321 blocks sha256/caching_sha2 cleartext, so impact is limited to crackable native/ed25519 hashes, not plaintext. Verified by reading only.

finding.claim: With allowPublicKeyRetrieval enabled, the RSA public key is taken from the server with no pinning, and the password is encrypted to that key, so an on-path attacker on a non-TLS connection recovers the password.
finding.source: Server-supplied RSA key in the public-key response (on-path attacker on plaintext connection)
finding.sink: Password encrypted under attacker-chosen RSA key (sendSha256PwdPacket)

trace.note: allowPublicKeyRetrieval gate (opt-in)
publicKey taken from server packet without pinning
password encrypted to that key
same pattern for caching_sha2

finding.guards_checked: Opt-in flag only; no TLS on this path; no key pinning. Documented tradeoff, low severity.
